description: The device-pairing contract's golden cases. core/test/pairing.test.js asserts the JS reproduces every one, and mobile/ClawTests/PairingParityTests.swift asserts the Swift port does, so both clients read the same gateway close into the same state, pull the same requestId out of the same reason, and move through the same four phases. The tokens and ids here are examples.
why: The `close` cases pin the one thing a client must not get wrong: pairing is code 1008 AND a pairing reason, so a 1008 with a non-pairing reason and a close on any other code are NOT pairing and stay ordinary failures. Getting that wrong would show a pairing screen for a dropped connection, or hide a real pairing gate behind a network message.
The `requestId` cases pin the strict id pattern: a well-formed id is read, and a reason with no id, or with an id that would not pass the pattern, yields null rather than arbitrary text on a screen.
The `phase` cases pin the phase moves, and that a non-pairing close is `failed` while a pairing close is `pairing-required`.

The `phase` cases pin the anti-flap rule: a `connect` from pairing-required STAYS pairing-required. A retry attempt happens underneath the pairing screen while the device is still unapproved, and pulling the visible state back to `connecting` on every retry (only to return to `pairing-required` on the next close) is what made the screen flap.

The `phase` cases also pin the anti-FLICKER rule, which is a level below the flap: an `open` while pairing-required HOLDS the screen, and only a `confirm` clears it. A 1008 pairing close is deliverable only after a WebSocket handshake completes, so the gateway genuinely opens the socket and then closes it 1008 on every retry, and the page's socket fires `open` before the close. Clearing the screen on that `open` tore the overlay away for the gap between the open and the close, once per retry, which exposed the reloading page underneath and was the flicker. So an unconfirmed open holds, and only an open that SURVIVES the settle window without a pairing close (a `confirm`) is the approval, which is auto-recovery. A `confirm` from any other phase is a no-op.

The `phase` cases also pin the moves that do NOT come from a first connect, because the pairing screen covering only a first connection is the failure this contract exists to make impossible: a pairing close from `authenticated` is `pairing-required`, exactly as it is from `connecting`. A session that was established, approved and working, and then had its approval revoked server-side, is refused with the same 1008 close, and a client that only ever entered pairing from its initial connecting phase showed that user a dead app with no explanation.

The `sequence` cases pin both rules at the level they happened: a run of retries, each a `connect`, an `open`, and another pairing `close`, must leave the visible phase on `pairing-required` throughout and never once pass through `connecting` OR `authenticated`. Passing through `authenticated` on a retry's open is the flicker; passing through `connecting` on a retry's connect is the flap. Only a `confirm` (an approved socket that survived) or a non-pairing close ends the wait. Two of them start from `authenticated`, which is the revocation path: the same run of retries, entered from a working session rather than from a cold start.
The `command` cases pin the real instruction: the exact `openclaw devices approve <id>` with an id, and the `--latest` form without one.

The `routing` cases pin where a pairing close sends the reader: the pairing screen for a first connection, and the settings surface on the gateways tab for a session that was already approved and has had its approval revoked. A client that gets this wrong either buries a revocation behind a screen about setup, or shows a setup screen to someone whose session was working a moment ago.

close.name: 1008 with a first-connection reason and an id is pairing

input.reason: pairing required: device is not approved yet (requestId: req-7f3a2b)

close.name: 1008 with a first-connection reason and no id is still pairing
1008 with a scope-upgrade reason is scope-upgrade, not the broader not-paired
1008 with a role-upgrade reason is role-upgrade
1008 with a metadata-upgrade reason is metadata-upgrade

input.reason: device metadata change pending approval (requestId: req-meta-3)

close.name: 1008 with a non-pairing reason is not pairing
1008 with an empty reason is not pairing
an abnormal close (1006) is never pairing, even with a pairing-looking reason
a normal close (1000) is not pairing
a missing code is not pairing

requestId.name: a well-formed id is read
requestId.input: pairing required: device is not approved yet (requestId: req-7f3a2b)

requestId.name: an id with the allowed punctuation is read
a reason with no id yields null
an id starting with punctuation fails the pattern and yields null

phase.name: a pairing close from connecting is pairing-required
a non-pairing close from connecting is failed
open while pairing-required HOLDS the screen, it is unconfirmed until confirm
confirm while pairing-required clears the screen, the approved socket survived
confirm from connecting is a no-op, there is no held open to confirm
a retry connect while pairing-required holds the screen, it does NOT drop to connecting
a pairing close while already pairing-required stays pairing-required
a non-pairing close while pairing-required ends the wait as an ordinary failure
a load failure is failed, not pairing-required
a pairing close from an established session is pairing-required, not an ordinary failure
a non-pairing close from an established session is an ordinary failure
a reconnect from an established session is connecting, the gateway may simply have moved
an open from an established session is authenticated, there is no screen to protect
an unknown event leaves the phase unchanged

sequence.name: the pairing screen does not flicker across repeated retries while waiting
an approval that lands after several retries ends the wait, and only on confirm
a revocation of an established session holds the pairing screen through the retries, and never returns to the connected state
a revoked session that is approved again recovers on its own, and only on confirm

routing.name: a first connection routes to the pairing screen, there is nothing else to look at
a pairing close that arrives after a failure is still a first connection
a revoked session routes to the settings surface, the gateway itself is the first question
no pairing entry has no route, so nothing moves the reader

command.name: with an id, the exact approve command
with no id, the latest form
an id that fails the pattern falls back to the latest form
